We need to determine if "Bob is green" follows from given facts and rules.

We have facts:

- Bob is kind.
- Bob is not nice.
- Bob is not round.
- Bob is smart.
- Erin is not green.

- If Bob is not young and Bob is not cold then Bob is round.

We need to see if Bob is green can be derived.

Goal: Bob is green.

We can try to derive Bob is green via known rules.

Rules:

1) All young things are cold. (Young -> Cold)
2) Cold things are green. (Cold -> Green)
3) If something is kind and not smart then it is green. (Kind ∧ ¬Smart -> Green)
4) If Erin is round and Erin is nice then Erin is not green. (ErinRound ∧ ErinNice -> ¬ErinGreen)
5) All kind things are young. (Kind -> Young)
6) If Bob is not young and Bob is not cold then Bob is round. (¬BobYoung ∧ ¬BobCold -> BobRound)

Facts: Bob is kind, Bob is not nice, Bob is not round, Bob is smart, etc.

We need to see if we can derive Bob is green.

From Bob is kind (fact). From rule 5 (All kind things are young) we can derive Bob is young.

Bob is young -> by rule 1 (Young -> Cold) we get Bob is cold.

Bob is cold -> by rule 2 (Cold -> Green) we get Bob is green.

Thus Bob is green follows.

Check any contradictions? Let's verify each step.

Rule: All kind things are young. So Bob is young.

Thus we have Bob is young.

Rule: All young things are cold. So Bob is cold.

Rule: Cold things are green. So Bob is green.

Thus Bob is green is derived.

Thus answer: True.

Bob is smart: The rule "If something is kind and not smart then it is green" does not apply because Bob is smart (so antecedent false). Not needed.

Thus Bob is green is derivable.

Thus answer: True.
